newsitem.title: SWAZILAND: SOCCER-MOZAMBIQUE THRASH SWAZLAND IN COSAFA CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MOZAMBIQUE THRASH SWAZLAND IN COSAFA CUP.

text.p: Striker Adelino marked his return to international football with a hat-trick as Mozambique thrashed Swaziland 4-0 away in the first round of the new Cosafa Castle Cup at the Somholo stadium in the Ezulwini Valley on Sunday.

The 28-year-old striker, a late inclusion in the squad after eight years without a cap, scored two goals in six minutes in the first half and then completed his hat-trick with 20 minutes left to propel the Mozambicans into the final stage of the compettion being organised by the Confederation of Southern African Football Associations (Cosafa).
Adelino had Mozambique ahead in the 36th minute against their neighbours with a tap-in from a free-kick and added his second in the 42nd minute with a free header at the back post.
Defender Sergio Faife provided Adelino's third in the 70th minute with a short free-kick which the striker tucked.
Substitute Eurico, playing in his third international, got the fourth goal with a header at the back post as the Swazi defence made no effort to deny him.

The heavy home defeat sparked fighting between rival fans in the tightly-packed stands at the small stadium. Opposing supporters pelted each other with beer cans at regular intervals throughout the match.

Mozambique now join Malawi, who won 4-1 away in Botswana on Saturday, in the final round group competition of the tournament, designed to give southern African countries more international competition and experience.

Swaziland: 1-Frazer France; 2-Moses Dlamini, 3-Oscar Simelane, 4-Dumisane Mdluli, 5-Philip Vilakati; 6-Muzi Maphalala, 7-Celemusa Vilakati (14-Ricky Saulos 64th minute), 8-Tholeni Nkambule (13-John Maseko 46th), 9-Vusi Mahlalela, 10-Haiso Dlamini (12-iza Dlamini 46th), 11-Themba Shongwe.
